1:   Arjuna.
2:   Fain would I better know, Thou Glorious One!
3:   The very truth--Heart's Lord!--of Sannyas,
4:   Abstention; and  enunciation, Lord!
5:   Tyaga; and what separates these twain!
6: 
7:   Krishna.
8:   The poets rightly teach that Sannyas
9:   Is the foregoing of all acts which spring
10:   Out of desire; and their wisest say
11:   Tyaga is renouncing fruit of acts.
12: 
13:   There be among the saints some who have held
14:   All action sinful, and to be renounced;
15:   And some who answer, "Nay! the goodly acts--
16:   As worship, penance, alms--must be performed!"
17:   Hear now My sentence, Best of Bharatas!
18: 
19:   'Tis well set forth, O Chaser of thy Foes!
20:   Renunciation is of threefold form,
21:   And Worship, Penance, Alms, not to be stayed;
22:   Nay, to be gladly done; for all those three
23:   Are purifying waters for true souls!
24: 
25:   Yet must be practised even those high works
26:   In yielding up attachment, and all fruit
27:   Produced by works. This is My judgment, Prince!
28:   This My insuperable and fixed decree!
29: 
30:   Abstaining from a work by right prescribed
31:   Never is meet! So to abstain doth spring
32:   From "Darkness," and Delusion teacheth it.
33:   Abstaining from a work grievous to flesh,
34:   When one saith "'Tis unpleasing!" this is null!
35:   Such an one acts from "passion;" nought of gain
36:   Wins his Renunciation! But, Arjun!
37:   Abstaining from attachment to the work,
38:   Abstaining from rewardment in the work,
39:   While yet one doeth it full faithfully,
40:   Saying, "Tis right to do!" that is "true " act
41:   And abstinence! Who doeth duties so,
42:   Unvexed if his work fail, if it succeed
43:   Unflattered, in his own heart justified,
44:   Quit of debates and doubts, his is "true" act:
45:   For, being in the body, none may stand
46:   Wholly aloof from act; yet, who abstains
47:   From profit of his acts is abstinent.
48: 
49:   The fruit of labours, in the lives to come,
50:   Is threefold for all men,--Desirable,
51:   And Undesirable, and mixed of both;
52:   But no fruit is at all where no work was.
53: 
54:   Hear from me, Long-armed Lord! the makings five
55:   Which go to every act, in Sankhya taught
56:   As necessary. First the force; and then
57:   The agent; next, the various instruments;
58:   Fourth, the especial effort; fifth, the God.
59:   What work soever any mortal doth
60:   Of body, mind, or speech, evil or good,
61:   By these five doth he that. Which being thus,
62:   Whoso, for lack of knowledge, seeth himself
63:   As the sole actor, knoweth nought at all
64:   And seeth nought. Therefore, I say, if one--
65:   Holding aloof from self--with unstained mind
66:   Should slay all yonder host, being bid to slay,
67:   He doth not slay; he is not bound thereby!
68: 
69:   Knowledge, the thing known, and the mind which knows,
70:   These make the threefold starting-ground of act.
71:   The act, the actor, and the instrument,
72:   These make the threefold total of the deed.
73:   But knowledge, agent, act, are differenced
74:   By three dividing qualities. Hear now
75:   Which be the qualities dividing them.
76: 
77:   There is "true" Knowledge. Learn thou it is this:
78:   To see one changeless Life in all the Lives,
79:   And in the Separate, One Inseparable.
80:   There is imperfect Knowledge: that which sees
81:   The separate existences apart,
82:   And, being separated, holds them real.
83:   There is false Knowledge: that which blindly clings
84:   To one as if 'twere all, seeking no Cause,
85:   Deprived of light, narrow, and dull, and "dark."
86: 
87:   There is "right" Action: that which being enjoined--
88:   Is wrought without attachment, passionlessly,
89:   For duty, not for love, nor hate, nor gain.
90:   There is "vain" Action: that which men pursue
91:   Aching to satisfy desires, impelled
92:   By sense of self, with all-absorbing stress:
93:   This is of Rajas--passionate and vain.
94:   There is "dark" Action: when one doth a thing
95:   Heedless of issues, heedless of the hurt
96:   Or wrong for others, heedless if he harm
97:   His own soul--'tis of Tamas, black and bad!
98: 
99:   There is the "rightful"doer. He who acts
100:   Free from self-seeking, humble, resolute,
101:   Steadfast, in good or evil hap the same,
102:   Content to do aright-he "truly" acts.
103:   There is th' "impassioned" doer. He that works
104:   From impulse, seeking profit, rude and bold
105:   To overcome, unchastened; slave by turns
106:   Of sorrow and of joy: of Rajas he!
107:   And there be evil doers; loose of heart,
108:   Low-minded, stubborn, fraudulent, remiss,
109:   Dull, slow, despondent--children of the "dark."
110: 
111:   Hear, too, of Intellect and Steadfastness
112:   The threefold separation, Conqueror-Prince!
113:   How these are set apart by Qualities.
114: 
115:   Good is the Intellect which comprehends
116:   The coming forth and going back of life,
117:   What must be done, and what must not be done,
118:   What should be feared, and what should not be feared,
119:   What binds and what emancipates the soul:
120:   That is of Sattwan, Prince! of "soothfastness."
121:   Marred is the Intellect which, knowing right
122:   And knowing wrong, and what is well to do
123:   And what must not be done, yet understands
124:   Nought with firm mind, nor as the calm truth is:
125:   This is of Rajas, Prince! and "passionate!"
126:   Evil is Intellect which, wrapped in gloom,
127:   Looks upon wrong as right, and sees all things
128:   Contrariwise of Truth. O Pritha's Son!
129:   That is of Tamas, "dark" and desperate!
130: 
131:   Good is the steadfastness whereby a man
132:   Masters his beats of heart, his very breath
133:   Of life, the action of his senses; fixed
134:   In never-shaken faith and piety:
135:   That is of Sattwan, Prince! "soothfast" and fair!
136:   Stained is the steadfastness whereby a man
137:   Holds to his duty, purpose, effort, end,
138:   For life's sake, and the love of goods to gain,
139:   Arjuna! 'tis of Rajas, passion-stamped!
140:   Sad is the steadfastness wherewith the fool
141:   Cleaves to his sloth, his sorrow, and his fears,
142:   His folly and despair. This--Pritha's Son!--
143:   Is born of Tamas, "dark" and miserable!
144: 
145: 
146:   Hear further, Chief of Bharatas! from Me
147:   The threefold kinds of Pleasure which there be.
148: 
149:   Good Pleasure is the pleasure that endures,
150:   Banishing pain for aye; bitter at first
151:   As poison to the soul, but afterward
152:   Sweet as the taste of Amrit. Drink of that!
153:   It springeth in the Spirit's deep content.
154:   And painful Pleasure springeth from the bond
155:   Between the senses and the sense-world. Sweet
156:   As Amrit is its first taste, but its last
157:   Bitter as poison. 'Tis of Rajas, Prince!
158:   And foul and "dark" the Pleasure is which springs
159:   From sloth and sin and foolishness; at first
160:   And at the last, and all the way of life
161:   The soul bewildering. 'Tis of Tamas, Prince!
162: 
163:   For nothing lives on earth, nor 'midst the gods
164:   In utmost heaven, but hath its being bound
165:   With these three Qualities, by Nature framed.
166: 
167:   The work of Brahmans, Kshatriyas, Vaisyas,
168:   And Sudras, O thou Slayer of thy Foes!
169:   Is fixed by reason of the Qualities
170:   Planted in each:
171: 
172:   A Brahman's virtues, Prince!
173:   Born of his nature, are serenity,
174:   Self-mastery, religion, purity,
175:   Patience, uprightness, learning, and to know
176:   The truth of things which be. A Kshatriya's pride,
177:   Born of his nature, lives in valour, fire,
178:   Constancy, skilfulness, spirit in fight,
179:   And open-handedness and noble mien,
180:   As of a lord of men. A Vaisya's task,
181:   Born with his nature, is to till the ground,
182:   Tend cattle, venture trade. A Sudra's state,
183:   Suiting his nature, is to minister.
184: 
185:   Whoso performeth--diligent, content--
186:   The work allotted him, whate'er it be,
187:   Lays hold of perfectness! Hear how a man
188:   Findeth perfection, being so content:
189:   He findeth it through worship--wrought by work--
190:   Of Him that is the Source of all which lives,
191:   Of HIM by Whom the universe was stretched.
192: 
193:   Better thine own work is, though done with fault,
194:   Than doing others' work, ev'n excellently.
195:   He shall not fall in sin who fronts the task
196:   Set him by Nature's hand! Let no man leave
197:   His natural duty, Prince! though it bear blame!
198:   For every work hath blame, as every flame
199:   Is wrapped in smoke! Only that man attains
200:   Perfect surcease of work whose work was wrought
201:   With mind unfettered, soul wholly subdued,
202:   Desires for ever dead, results renounced.
203: 
204:   Learn from me, Son of Kunti! also this,
205:   How one, attaining perfect peace, attains
206:   BRAHM, the supreme, the highest height of all!
207: 
208:   Devoted--with a heart grown pure, restrained
209:   In lordly self-control, forgoing wiles
210:   Of song and senses, freed from love and hate,
211:   Dwelling 'mid solitudes, in diet spare,
212:   With body, speech, and will tamed to obey,
213:   Ever to holy meditation vowed,
214:   From passions liberate, quit of the Self,
215:   Of arrogance, impatience, anger, pride;
216:   Freed from surroundings, quiet, lacking nought--
217:   Such an one grows to oneness with the BRAHM;
218:   Such an one, growing one with BRAHM, serene,
219:   Sorrows no more, desires no more; his soul,
220:   Equally loving all that lives, loves well
221:   Me, Who have made them, and attains to Me.
222:   By this same love and worship doth he know
223:   Me as I am, how high and wonderful,
224:   And knowing, straightway enters into Me.
225:   And whatsoever deeds he doeth--fixed
226:   In Me, as in his refuge--he hath won
227:   For ever and for ever by My grace
228:   Th' Eternal Rest! So win thou! In thy thoughts
229:   Do all thou dost for Me! Renounce for Me!
230:   Sacrifice heart and mind and will to Me!
231:   Live in the faith of Me! In faith of Me
232:   All dangers thou shalt vanquish, by My grace;
233:   But, trusting to thyself and heeding not,
234:   Thou can'st but perish! If this day thou say'st,
235:   Relying on thyself, "I will not fight!"
236:   Vain will the purpose prove! thy qualities
237:   Would spur thee to the war. What thou dost shun,
238:   Misled by fair illusions, thou wouldst seek
239:   Against thy will, when the task comes to thee
240:   Waking the promptings in thy nature set.
241:   There lives a Master in the hearts of men
242:   Maketh their deeds, by subtle  pulling--strings,
243:   Dance to what tune HE will. With all thy soul
244:   Trust Him, and take Him for thy succour, Prince!
245:   So--only so, Arjuna!--shalt thou gain--
246:   By grace of Him--the uttermost repose,
247:   The Eternal Place!
248: 
249:   Thus hath been opened thee
250:   This Truth of Truths, the Mystery more hid
251:   Than any secret mystery. Meditate!
252:   And--as thou wilt--then act!
253: 
254:   Nay! but once more
255:   Take My last word, My utmost meaning have!
256:   Precious thou art to Me; right well-beloved!
257:   Listen! I tell thee for thy comfort this.
258:   Give Me thy heart! adore Me! serve Me! cling
259:   In faith and love and reverence to Me!
260:   So shalt thou come to Me! I promise true,
261:   For thou art sweet to Me!
262: 
263:   And let go those--
264:   Rites and writ duties! Fly to Me alone!
265:   Make Me thy single refuge! I will free
266:   Thy soul from all its  sins! Be of good cheer!
267: 
268:   [Hide, the holy Krishna saith,
269:   This from him that hath no faith,
270:   Him that worships not, nor seeks
271:   Wisdom's teaching when she speaks:
272:   Hide it from all men who mock;
273:   But, wherever, 'mid the flock
274:   Of My lovers, one shall teach
275:   This  divinest, wisest, speech--
276:   Teaching in the faith to bring
277:   Truth to them, and offering
278:   Of all honour unto Me--
279:   Unto Brahma cometh he!
280:   Nay, and nowhere shall ye find
281:   Any man of all mankind
282:   Doing dearer deed for Me;
283:   Nor shall any dearer be
284:   In My earth. Yea, furthermore,
285:   Whoso reads this converse o'er,
286:   Held by Us upon the plain,
287:   Pondering piously and fain,
288:   He hath paid Me sacrifice!
289:   (Krishna speaketh in this wise!)
290:   Yea, and whoso, full of faith,
291:   Heareth wisely what it saith,
292:   Heareth meekly,--when he dies,
293:   Surely shall his spirit rise
294:   To those regions where the Blest,
295:   Free of flesh, in joyance rest.]
296: 
297:   Hath this been heard by thee, O Indian Prince!
298:   With mind intent? hath all the ignorance--
299:   Which bred thy trouble--vanished, My Arjun?
300: 
301:   Arjuna.
302:   Trouble and ignorance are gone! the Light
303:   Hath come unto me, by Thy favour, Lord!
304:   Now am I fixed! my doubt is fled away!
305:   According to Thy word, so will I do!
306: 
307:   Sanjaya.
308:   Thus gathered I the gracious speech of Krishna, O my King!
309:   Thus have I told, with heart a-thrill, this wise and wondrous thing
310:   By great Vyasa's learning writ, how Krishna's self made known
311:   The Yoga, being Yoga's Lord. So is the high truth shown!
312:   And aye, when I remember, O Lord my King, again
313:   Arjuna and the God in talk, and all this holy strain,
314:   Great is my gladness: when I muse that splendour, passing speech,
315:   Of Hari, visible and plain, there is no tongue to reach
316:   My marvel and my love and bliss. O Archer-Prince! all hail!
317:   O Krishna, Lord of Yoga! surely there shall not fail
318:   Blessing, and victory, and power, for Thy most mighty sake,
319:   Where this song comes of Arjun, and how with God he spake.
320: 
321:   HERE ENDS, WITH CHAPTER XVIII.,
322:   Entitled "Mokshasanyasayog,"
323:   Or "The Book of Religion by Deliverance and Renunciation,"
324:   THE BHAGAVAD-GITA.

witnesses.text: 18.1 Arjuna said I desire to know severally, O mighty-armed, the essence or truth of renunciation, O Hrishikesa, as also of abandonment, O slayer of Kesi.

witnesses.text: 18.1 "Arjuna asked: O mighty One! I desire to know how relinquishment is distinguished from renunciation.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 18.1 Arjuna said O mighty-armed Hrsikesa, O slayer of (the demon) Kesi, I want to know serverally the truth about sannyasa as also about tyaga.

Krishna.

  Is the foregoing of all acts which spring

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 18.2 The Blessed Lord said The sages understand Sannyasa to be the renunciation of action with desire; the wise declare the abandonment of the fruits of all actions as Tyaga.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 18.2 Lord Shri Krishna replied: The sages say that renunciation means forgoing an action which springs from desire; and relinquishing means the surrender of its fruit.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 18.2 The Blessed Lord said The learned ones know sannyasa to be the giving up of actions done with a desire for reward. The adepts call the abandonment of the results of all works as tyaga.

arnold.content:
Yet must be practised even those high works
  In yielding up attachment, and all fruit
  Produced by works. This is My judgment, Prince!
  This My insuperable and fixed decree!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 18.6 But even these actions should be performed leaving aside attachment and the desire for rewards, O Arjuna; this is My certain and best conviction.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 18.6 But they should be done with detachment and without thought of recompense. This is my final judgment.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 18.6 But even these actions have to be undertaken by renouncing attachment and (hankering for) results. This is My firm and best conclusion, O Parhta.
